analysis.title: Americas Business & Information Services: What's Powering Your Services Recap - 11/6/26
key_insights: Investor feedback this week was negative on companies with softer leading indicators, weaker outlooks or higher investment spend despite quarterly beats. It was favorable toward CLVT, ULS, BCO and VRSK on stronger operating momentum and forward indicators.

Information Services averaged +4% this week and -15% YTD, with CLVT +41%, TRU +8% and VRSK +8% up and IT -13% and MH -16% down. Business Services averaged 0% this week and +14% YTD, with ROL +12%, HRB +7% and BCO +7% up and IRM -9% and PXED -10% down. The S&P 500 fell 3% this week.

Gartner (IT, Neutral): 3Q revenue, EBITDA margin and EPS beat and full-year guidance was raised. Ex-US federal contract value grew only 2.8% y/y, and Gartner no longer expects to reach its prior 4% year-end target. Insights is 86% of revenue, so Conferences and Consulting strength cannot offset the slower recovery.

GS cut Gartner contract value growth forecasts to 4.5% in 2027 and 6% in 2028, from 6% and 7%, against 3% in 2026. The guidance raise partly reflects NCVI arriving earlier in the quarter and analyst costs that will return as headcount is rebuilt.

Thomson Reuters (TRI, Buy): 3Q revenue and EBITDA beat GS estimates and the full-year organic growth guide was raised on the Global Print divestiture. Big 3 organic growth was 10% y/y for a second quarter. 4Q organic growth is guided to about 8% and 2027 operating leverage will be reinvested in AI, which limits near-term margin expansion.
Gen AI-enabled products reached 34% of TRI ACV, up from 30% in 2Q and 24% a year ago. The Global Print divestiture adds 60-70 bps to TRI's organic growth profile.

Phoenix Education (PXED, Neutral): AI search pressure on B2C new starts is now flowing through enrollment and revenue. F2027 revenue guidance is 8% below GS's prior forecast and implies a 3% decline, so the recovery shifts to F2028. F2027 EBITDA guidance of $225-240mn compares with consensus of $261mn, and about 90 bps of EBITDA margin contraction is expected.

Iron Mountain (IRM, Buy): AFFO/share beat and 2026 guidance rose, but revenue was in line and the 4Q outlook implies further growth moderation. Record quarterly leasing of 102 MW supports 20%+ data center revenue growth in 2027, with signed backlog providing nearly 40% further growth once developed.

IRM's India leasing was 74 MW at yields 200-300 bps above its typical 10-12% unlevered return range at the low end. ALM is projected at 25%+ organic growth in 2027, and the US Treasury digital contract ramps from $40-45mn in 2026 to $100-150mn in 2027.

McGraw Hill (MH, Buy): F2Q revenue and EPS beat but EBITDA margin was below expectations and F2027 guidance was reiterated. Weaker math capture rates are the main execution risk. Recovery depends on California pilots converting and Texas districts returning to commercial offerings. Higher Education should keep mid-single-digit growth and early ELA capture rates are above the 25-30% target.

Fair Isaac (FICO, Buy): F4Q revenue grew 27% y/y with 600 bps of EBITDA margin expansion, both above consensus. FICO withheld F2027 guidance because mortgage pricing is moving from uniform to bespoke arrangements. Mortgage originations fell high-single-digits y/y and mix shifted to lower-priced HELOCs.

FICO Software Platform ARR rose 72% y/y with NRR of 156%. Direct license agreements cover reseller partners representing about 73% of mortgage reseller volume. GS expects double-digit annual EPS growth supported by renewed buybacks.

Verisk (VRSK, Neutral): 3Q revenue, EBITDA margin and EPS beat and the full-year guide was reiterated. OCC revenue growth returned to 7.4% y/y, inside the 6-8% medium-term target, with subscriptions up 8% OCC and about 84% of revenue. Transactional strength from Life Solutions services and data-pull overages should moderate in 4Q.

Brink's (BCO, Buy): 3Q revenue missed but EBITDA margin and EPS beat and the full-year guide was reaffirmed. DRS/AMS revenue grew 16%+ organically, up from 14% in 2Q, and was a record 32% of revenue. BCO now expects the NCR Atleos deal to close in early January 2027, nearly a quarter earlier than planned, and sees cost synergies beyond the original $200mn target.

NCR Atleos (NATL, Not Rated): 3Q revenue missed but EBITDA margin and EPS beat. ATMaaS revenue grew 24% y/y and software revenue 18%, while Self-Service Banking hardware fell 20% and Network revenue fell 2% on lower crypto transaction volumes. NATL gave no outlook, will not host a call and suspended its buyback ahead of the Brink's deal.

Clarivate (CLVT, Neutral): 3Q shows improving recurring revenue, and IP ACV returned to positive growth for the first time in more than three years. The $488mn LS&H sale leaves a roughly $2bn revenue business that is 93% recurring and supports about $875mn of 2026 debt reduction. CLVT lowered 2026 organic ACV, recurring revenue and FCF guidance after the divestiture, and ACV growth of 1.8% is below roughly 3% pricing.

ADT (Not Rated): 3Q revenue rose 3.9% y/y to $1,349mn on a 32% rise in installation revenue. EBITDA margin contracted 280 bps y/y to 49.3% and gross revenue attrition rose 10 bps to 13.1%. ADT agreed to be acquired by Thrive Holdings for $10.00/share in cash, expected to close in 1Q 2027, and withdrew its prior guidance.

UL Solutions (ULS, Neutral): 3Q revenue, EBITDA margin and EPS beat and full-year organic growth guidance was raised. GS is confident in at least mid-single-digit organic growth into 2027, led by Industrial and data center testing demand. Muted Advisory trends, depressed Risk & Compliance Software margins and Eurofins E&E integration costs should constrain 2027 margin expansion.

Temp staffing: October temp penetration rose to 1.59% from 1.58% and temp jobs rose 3.0% y/y, accelerating from 1.4%. Penetration is still below the 1.92% pre-COVID level. About 55% of US temp roles are white-collar and exposed to AI disintermediation, so GS expects a less robust cycle than prior ones.

GS keeps Sell on Robert Half, Neutral on Manpower and a positive view on Korn Ferry. After a non-deal roadshow on 11/2, GS was incrementally more positive on RHI's staffing and Protiviti recovery but remains Sell because the recovery is gradual and SMB demand lags.

Ratings: global debt issuance fell 29% y/y in October after +5% in September but is still up 7% YTD. GS reiterates Buy on SPGI and MCO and expects SPGI Ratings and MCO MIS revenue each up about 8% in 2026, with 4Q relatively flat y/y.
Initial jobless claims fell to 189k for the week ending 10/31, below the FactSet consensus of 196k. GS calls a tight labor market incrementally positive for temp staffers MAN and RHI.

Valuations: Information Services trades at 13.6x NTM EV/EBITDA and 18.8x NTM P/E, and Business Services at 9.7x and 17.8x. The S&P 500 is at 13.1x and 17.7x. NTM multiples for the group have recently trended lower.

CY2026 consensus EPS is broadly stable YTD with wide dispersion. The largest upward revisions are VSTS +77.6%, MH +19.5% and PBI +18.8%. The largest cuts are KLC -82.5%, BV -34.2%, RHI -22.8% and TRI -10.5%.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q beat and guidance raise overshadowed by slower Insights contract value recovery. GS cut 2027 and 2028 CV growth forecasts and sees balanced risk/reward.
Big 3 organic growth of 10% and rising Gen AI product share support the longer-term view. Softer 4Q growth and 2027 AI reinvestment temper near-term earnings.
AI search pressure pushes the recovery to F2028 and F2027 guidance is 8% below GS's revenue forecast. GS sees balanced risk-reward after the reset.
Record 102 MW of data center leasing, ALM and digital solutions growth support a multi-year outlook despite 4Q growth moderation.
Higher Education strength, the F2028 ELA cycle and AI monetization remain intact. Math capture rates are the near-term risk.
Revenue and margin beat with Software Platform growth. F2027 guidance was withheld during the mortgage pricing transition.
Organic growth returned to its medium-term range on durable subscriptions. Transactional headwinds and unclear enterprise AI timing balance this.
DRS/AMS momentum and an earlier NCR Atleos close strengthen the earnings outlook.
Operating trajectory is improving after the LS&H divestiture, but a durable recovery needs stronger volumes, pipeline conversion and cash conversion.
Beat-and-raise with volume-led growth and record margins, balanced by valuation, integration costs and Advisory headwinds.
Staffing recovery is gradual, SMB demand lags and AI remains a longer-term demand and valuation uncertainty, despite improving Protiviti and staffing volumes.
Improving underlying demand and share gains are balanced by gross margin pressure and limited near-term earnings conversion.
Improving organic demand, cross-selling and AMS should increase contracted revenue visibility and support sustained growth.
Diversified growth across Market Intelligence, Indices and Energy, plus potential value from the CapIQ strategic review.
Structural ratings tailwinds and resilient high-single-digit organic growth in Moody's Analytics.

sector_views.rationale: Average NTM EV/EBITDA of 13.6x and P/E of 18.8x, with group multiples trending lower. Stock reactions split on forward indicators and AI investment spend.
Average NTM EV/EBITDA of 9.7x and P/E of 17.8x. Temp staffing is stabilizing but recovering gradually and is exposed to AI disintermediation in white-collar roles.
AI-related financing and a $7.2tn US and EMEA refinancing pipeline through 2031 support medium-term issuance and ratings revenue, despite a weak October.

earnings_insights: MH reported F2Q 2027 EPS of $0.75 vs FactSet consensus of $0.72 (reported), and guided F2027 EBITDA to $750-790mn vs consensus of $772mn.
VRSK reported 3Q 2026 EPS of $1.96 vs FactSet consensus of $1.92 (reported), and guided 2026 EPS to $7.45-7.75 vs consensus of $7.71.
IRM reported 3Q 2026 AFFO/share of $1.53 vs FactSet consensus of $1.48, and guided 2026 EPS to $5.94-6.00 vs consensus of $5.92.
FICO reported F4Q 2026 EPS of $11.10 vs FactSet consensus of $10.69 (reported) and withheld F2027 guidance.
NATL reported 3Q 2026 EPS of $1.35 vs FactSet consensus of $1.19 (reported).
BCO reported 3Q 2026 EPS of $2.46 vs FactSet consensus of $2.21 (reported). Its guidance range implies 2026 EBITDA margins of 18.9-19.1% vs consensus of 18.9%.
PXED reported F4Q 2026 EPS of $1.07 in line with FactSet consensus of $1.07 (reported), and guided F2027 EBITDA to $225-240mn vs consensus of $261mn.
ADT reported 3Q 2026 EPS of $0.24 vs FactSet consensus of $0.23 (reported).
ULS reported 3Q 2026 EPS of $0.62 vs FactSet consensus of $0.61 (reported), and guided 2026 EBITDA margins to about 27.0% vs consensus of 27.3%.
TRI reported 3Q 2026 EPS of $0.81 vs FactSet consensus of $0.83 (reported, a miss), and guided 2026 EBITDA margins to about 39.0% vs consensus of 39.3%.
CLVT reported 3Q 2026 EPS of $0.19 vs FactSet consensus of $0.18 (reported), and guided 2026 EPS to $0.73-0.77 vs consensus of $0.74.
IT reported 3Q 2026 EPS of $3.59 vs FactSet consensus of $2.84 (reported), and guided 2026 EPS to at least $14.65 vs consensus of $14.47.
Upcoming reports and events: HRB F1Q earnings 11/9, FDS investor day and BV F4Q earnings 11/10, KLC 3Q earnings 11/12, MH investor day 11/18, MSCI 4Q earnings 1/26.

AI search disruption continues to pressure PXED B2C new starts with no meaningful SEO recovery assumed in F2027.
Weak math capture rates at MH, dependent on California pilots converting and Texas districts returning.

tension_points.bull_case: 3Q revenue, EBITDA margin and EPS beat, full-year guidance was raised, and Conferences and Consulting are bright spots.
tension_points.bear_case: Ex-US federal contract value grew only 2.8%, GTS and GBS new business fell 4% and 3%, and Insights is 86% of revenue. Part of the EBITDA upside reflects analyst costs that will return.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Gartner no longer expects to reach its prior 4% year-end contract value target. A faster than expected acceleration in Insights contract value would support the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: Big 3 organic growth of 10% for a second quarter, Gen AI products at 34% of ACV and the Global Print divestiture adds 60-70 bps to organic growth.
tension_points.bear_case: 4Q organic growth is guided to about 8% on tougher Reuters comparisons and 2027 operating leverage will be reinvested in AI, limiting near-term margin expansion.

tension_points.bull_case: Record 102 MW of leasing supports 20%+ data center revenue growth in 2027, with ALM projected at 25%+ organic growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Revenue was in line and the 4Q outlook implies further growth moderation.

tension_points.bull_case: 27% revenue growth, 600 bps of margin expansion, Platform ARR up 72% and bespoke pricing can preserve mortgage share.
tension_points.bear_case: F2027 guidance was withheld, mortgage originations fell high-single-digits y/y and future disclosure gives limited visibility into pricing realization.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Conforming opportunity for FICO Score 10T depends on GSE implementation, and loss of mortgage volume to VantageScore would undercut the thesis.

tension_points.bull_case: Guidance assumes no recovery in search, so upside is possible if conditions improve. Employer enrollment grew about 13% in F2026 and the new-program pipeline is the strongest since F2021.
tension_points.bear_case: AI search pressure is flowing through enrollment and revenue, F2027 revenue is guided to a 3% decline and EBITDA margin contracts about 90 bps.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Search conditions improving or SEO recovery would lift the F2027 outlook above guidance.

tension_points.bull_case: Temp penetration and temp jobs growth improved in October, with temp wage growth of 5.1% y/y outpacing permanent wages.
tension_points.bear_case: Penetration is near multi-year lows and about 55% of US temp roles are white-collar and exposed to AI disintermediation, so volume recovery lags pricing.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A meaningful volume recovery to match stronger pricing would challenge the cautious view on Robert Half.
